ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: ‘Named condition’ is the selected English label for a borrowed name for a condition, command, or named mode that speakers say one enters, leaves, possesses, or displays. Its proper-name use instead identifies the named person Sanmei; that person/title referent is kept separate.
EvidenceBody: The term occurs 4,852 times in 382 allowed texts. Huineng defines 'named condition of the single conduct' as 'at every place, while walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, always carry one straight mind' (一行三昧者，於一切處行住坐臥，常行一直心是也). The same address rejects the claim that 'not raising thought while constantly sitting unmoving is named condition of the single conduct' (常坐不動，妄不起心，即是一行三昧), saying that this understanding is like the insentient and blocks the Way. Mazu's record says that thought after thought becoming still is called 'named condition of the ocean seal,' which 'takes in all things as a hundred thousand different streams return together to the great sea' (喚作海印三昧攝一切法如百千異流同歸大海). It also says beings remain within 'named condition of the nature of the teaching' while dressing, eating, speaking, responding, using the six sense-roots, and carrying out every action (法性三昧中著衣喫飯言談祇對六根運用一切施為). Xuansha says that buddhas are people's 'self-receiving named condition' and that walking, standing, sitting, and lying down have never not been it; when asked what that named condition is, he replies, 'What use are so many modes of named condition?' (用如許多三昧作麼). The word therefore appears as the head of explicitly named states or domains whose predicates vary by text; this entry does not collapse those names into one imported definition.

EvidenceBody: These predicates belong to a named person, so this sense remains separate from lexical named-condition compounds. The witnesses place Master Sanmei in the precept and ordination family rather than defining the borrowed word.
